claude.sample_unit: escitalopram-related adverse event reports (129,427 FAERS + 6,614 JADER)

links.outcome: AUC of suicide-related AE prediction model applied cross-database versus after retraining on local database
links.effect: XGBoost AUC 0.8578 on FAERS; applied to JADER dropped to 0.6379; retraining on JADER restored AUC to 0.8365.
links.quote: Retraining on JADER restored performance (AUC = 0.8365), comparable to native-dataset performance.

links.outcome: Model performance when applied to a different database/population than developed on
links.effect: Cross-database application of the FAERS-trained XGBoost model to JADER caused substantial performance drop (AUC 0.8578 to 0.6379).
links.quote: XGBoost achieved the best performance on FAERS (AUC = 0.8578), but cross-database application to JADER caused substantial performance drop (AUC = 0.6379).

links.effect: XGBoost AUC was 0.8578 on FAERS but dropped to 0.6379 on JADER.
links.quote: XGBoost achieved the best performance on FAERS (AUC = 0.8578), but cross-database application to JADER caused substantial performance drop (AUC = 0.6379).

links.effect: Retraining on JADER restored performance to AUC = 0.8365, comparable to native-dataset performance.
links.quote: Retraining on JADER restored performance (AUC = 0.8365), comparable to native-dataset performance.

links.effect: Retraining on JADER restored AUC to 0.8365 from 0.6379 with cross-database application, comparable to native FAERS AUC of 0.8578.
links.quote: Retraining on JADER restored performance (AUC = 0.8365), comparable to native-dataset performance.

screen.reason: The study evaluates predictive models for drug adverse events and explicitly tests cross-database transportability and the impact of database-specific local retraining/adaptation to prevent performance drop.
